Data pipelines use typed Dataset classes, optimized DataLoader settings with pin_memory and persistent workers, and collate_fn for variable-length batches. Checkpointing saves model, optimizer, epoch, and loss state. Performance options include gradient checkpointing, torch.compile, and profiling with torch.profiler.

items.name: security-threat-model
items.author: openai
items.description: Turn your real repo layout, auth flows, and integrations into a prioritized threat model with abuse paths and mitigations before you harden or release.
items.summary: security-threat-model delivers actionable AppSec-grade threat modeling anchored to a repository or scoped path, not generic checklists. The workflow scopes and extracts the system model from repo evidence, derives trust boundaries, assets, and entry points, calibrates attacker capabilities, enumerates high-quality abuse paths, prioritizes with explicit likelihood and impact reasoning, validates assumptions with the user, recommends mitigations tied to components, and runs a quality check before finalizing. It separates runtime behavior from CI, build, dev tooling, and tests, and refuses to claim components or controls without evidence. Step six pauses for one to three targeted user questions on deployment, auth, exposure, and data sensitivity before the final report. Mitigations distinguish existing controls from recommendations with concrete implementation hints such as schema enforcement at gateways. Output follows references/prompt-template.md and writes to a file named repo-or-dir-name-threat-model.md. Risk guidance covers pre-auth RCE, auth bypass, cross-tenant access, and data exfiltration as high priority examples. Trigger only when users explicitly request threat modeling,.
highlights: Eight-step workflow from scoping through boundaries, threats, prioritization, user validation, mitigations, and QA.
Requires evidence-backed components, flows, and controls with explicit assumptions and open questions.
Pauses after threat ranking to confirm deployment, auth, exposure, and data sensitivity with the user.
Enumerates abuse paths mapped to assets and trust boundaries instead of generic checklist items.
Final Markdown report follows references/prompt-template.md output contract and named file convention.

items.name: jobs-to-be-done
items.author: wondelai
items.description: Uncover the real reasons customers will pay for a product by mapping functional, emotional, and social jobs-to-be-done.
items.summary: The jobs-to-be-done skill Discover what customers truly need by analyzing the "job" they hire your product to do. Use when the user mentions "customer discovery", "why customers churn", "what job does this solve", "competing against luck", "product-market fit", "switching behavior", "milkshake moment", or "functional vs emotional jobs". Also trigger when investigating why users choose competitors, designing features around real customer needs, or reframing product value propositions. Covers JTBD interviews, competition analysis, and jobs-oriented roadmaps. For product positioning, see obviously-awesome. For rapid validation, see design-sprint. Framework for discovering innovation based on a fundamental truth: customers don't buy products -- they "hire" them to do a specific job in their lives. Job to Be Done = the progress a customer wants to make in specific circumstances. Key elements of the definition: - Progress (not goal, not solution) -- the customer wants to move from the current state to a better one - Circumstances -- context determines the job, not customer attributes (demographics are useless) - Hiring/Firing -- the customer actively chooses a
highlights: Progress (not goal, not solution) -- the customer wants to move from the current state to a better one
Circumstances -- context determines the job, not customer attributes (demographics are useless)
Hiring/Firing -- the customer actively chooses a product for the "job"
Format: "When [circumstances], I want to [progress], so I can [outcome]"
Circumstances matter more than demographics -- the same person has different jobs in different situations

items.name: explore-data
items.author: anthropics
items.description: Quickly profile any new dataset, table or file and surface shape, quality issues and distribution patterns before writing analysis code.
items.summary: explore-data generates a comprehensive data profile for tables or uploaded files, revealing row/column counts, data types, grain, and quality metrics. Developers use it when encountering unfamiliar datasets to classify columns (identifier, dimension, metric, temporal, text, boolean, structural), detect issues (high nulls, duplicates, suspicious values), and discover patterns. The tool runs profiling queries against live warehouse tables or infers types from uploaded CSV/Excel/Parquet/JSON files, then surfaces null rates, cardinality ratios, value distributions, and flagged anomalies. Follow-up recommendations suggest specific trend analyses, distribution deep-dives, and correlation studies. Essential for data exploration workflows before building dashboards, reports, or analytics pipelines. Profiles table structure: row count, column types, primary keys, date range coverage, and data grain Classifies all columns by role - identifier, dimension, metric, temporal, text, boolean, structural Detects data quality issues: null
highlights: Profiles table structure: row count, column types, primary keys, date range coverage, and data grain
Classifies all columns by role - identifier, dimension, metric, temporal, text, boolean, structural
Detects data quality issues: null rates >5% or >20%, low/high cardinality surprises, duplicates, suspicious values, enco
Computes per-column stats: nulls, distinct counts, top/bottom values, min/max/mean/median for numerics, length and case
Recommends 3-5 follow-up analyses (trends, correlations, cohorts, distribution deep-dives, quality investigations)
